properties.description: Porous, nanofibrous material with hierarchical structure

nodes.name: ZIF-67 TPAs synthesis
nodes.procedure: ZIF-67 TPAs are directly grown on the surface of nickel foam (NF) via a facile reaction of Co(NO3)2 with 2-methylimidazole (MIM) in an aqueous solution at room temperature for 2 h. [33]
nodes.source_text: First, ZIF-67 TPAs are directly grown on the surface of nickel foam (NF) via a facile reaction of Co(NO3)2 with MIM in an aqueous solution, which takes place at room temperature in 2h. [33]

unit_operations.name: Growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: facile reaction of Co(NO3)2 with MIM in an aqueous solution at room temperature in 2h

nodes.name: Postsynthetic ligand exchange
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained ZIF-67 TPAs are immersed into the K4[Fe(CN)6] aqueous solution at room temperature and maintained for 8 h to allow the mild postsynthetic ligand exchange reaction of 2-methylimidazole (MIM) with K4[Fe(CN)6] to produce the mesoporous prussian blue analogue Co2[Fe(CN)6] (CoFe(II)-PBA) HTPAs.
nodes.source_text: In step I, the as-obtained ZIF-67 TPAs are then immersed into the K4[Fe(CN)6] aqueous solution at room temperature and maintained for 8h to allow the mild postsynthetic ligand exchange reaction...

unit_operations.name: Immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed into the K4[Fe(CN)6] aqueous solution at room temperature and maintained for 8h

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: By using NaH2PO2 as the phosphor source, the CoFe(II)-PBA HTPAs are phosphorized through a 2 h reaction in N2 atmosphere at 300°C, and the final product of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs are obtained.
nodes.source_text: In step II, by using NaH2PO2 as the phosphor source, the CoFe(II)-PBA HTPAs are phosphorized through a 2h reaction in N2 atmosphere at 300°C...

unit_operations.name: Phosphorization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: phosphorized through a 2h reaction in N2 atmosphere at 300°C

nodes.source_text: The water splitting activities of the as-prepared Fe-CoP HTPAs catalyst were first examined for HER in an alkaline solution (1 M KOH), with a conventional electrochemical three-electrode cell measured with a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹. As shown by the iR-corrected polarization curves in Figure 5a, the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit superior HER performance to CoP TPAs. To drive a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs require an overpotential of 98 mV while the overpotential for CoP TPAs is high up to 120 mV. ... the Tafel slope for the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs is measured as 69 mV dec⁻¹ ... the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit a much higher Cdl of 127.9 mF cm⁻² ... The chronoamperometric response at the fixed overpotential of 98 mV reveals the high stability of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs. Remarkably, as shown in Figure 5c, the current density is negligibly declined over 50 h

The OER performances of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs and CoP TPAs were also evaluated by using an electrochemical three-electrode cell with an alkaline solution (1 M KOH) and measuring with a scan rate of 1 mV s⁻¹. The polarization curves with iR correction of the as-prepared samples are presented in Figure 6a. ... the overpotential of 230 mV at the same current density of 10 mA cm⁻² ... the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit a much lower Tafel slope of 43 mV dec⁻¹ ... the Faradaic efficiency of the OER process occurring on the Fe-CoP HTPAs is determined to be about 96.1% ... The long-term stability of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs was examined by chronoamperometry at the fixed overpotential of 230 mV (Figure 6b). Remarkably, the change of the current density is negligible over 50 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: we further examine its potential for overall water splitting by utilizing the Fe-CoP catalyst as both the anode and the cathode in a two-electrode cell. The polarization curves for overall water splitting obtained in 1 M KOH with a scan rate of 1 mV s⁻¹ are shown in Figure 6c. As we can see, only a low cell voltage of 1.59 V is required for the Fe-CoP HTPAs to achieve the current density of 10 mA cm⁻². ... The chronopotentiometry result of the Fe-CoP HTPAs is shown in Figure 6d, which indicates the very stable current density over 50 h

To drive a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs require an overpotential of 98 mV while the overpotential for CoP TPAs is high up to 120 mV. ... the Tafel slope for the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs is measured as 69 mV dec⁻¹ much smaller than 90 mV dec⁻¹ of CoP TPAs ... the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit a much higher Cdl of 127.9 mF cm⁻², which is nearly 2.9 times that of CoP TPAs (43.7 mF cm⁻²)
The overpotential of CoP TPAs is determined to be 270 mV at the current density of 10 mA cm⁻². ... Compared with the value of 82 mV dec⁻¹ for CoP TPAs

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks of Fe-CoP HTPAs attributed to orthorhombic CoP (JCPDS 65-2593) with lattice parameters a=5.076Å, b=3.277Å, c=5.599Å, no iron phosphide impurity phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As confirmed by the XRD pattern in Figure S5 in the Supporting Information, the diffraction peaks of Fe-CoP HTPAs can be attributed to the characteristics of orthorhombic CoP (JCPDS card No. 65-2593, a = 5.076Å , b = 3.277Å , c = 5.599Å ), without any impurity phase of iron phosphide...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals hollow and porous structure with vertically aligned structural units and open voids inherited from CoFe(II)-PBA HTPAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Revealed by the SEM images in Figure 2a,b, the hollow and porous structure and the vertically aligned structural units are well inherited from the CoFe(II)-PBA HTPAs.

properties.features: porous structure, nanofibrous morphology, hierarchical texture
detailed nanofiber texture with porous surface
spongy, porous morphology with interconnected pores

nodes.characterization_summary: FIB-SEM confirms uniform hollow interior in all Fe-CoP TPAs after milling with gallium ion beam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2c,d, the Fe-CoP TPAs milled by FIB using gallium ion beam clearly present a totally different frame, from which uniform hollow interior can be observed...

properties.description: High-resolution scanning electron microscopy image showing nanostructured material with rough, porous morphology consisting of aggregated nanoparticles and clusters

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows shell composed of interconnected nanoparticles with large amount of mesopores distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnified TEM image (Figure 3b) clearly shows that the shell of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs is composed of many interconnected nanoparticles with a large amount of mesopores distributed.

properties.label: b
properties.description: SEM image with two panels showing microstructure

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm consistent with CoP (200) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 3c) of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs displays an interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm , which is consistent with the lattice distance of the CoP (200) plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern indexed to (011), (200), (211), (301) planes of CoP, indicating ternary Fe-Co-P compound.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the selected-area diffraction (SAED) pattern for hierarchical mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs (Figure 3d) can be well indexed into (011), (200), (211), and (301) plans of CoP...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS displays presence of Fe, Co, and P elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy dispersive X-ray spectrum (Figure S6, Supporting Information) of the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs displays the presence of Fe, Co, and P elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co, Fe, and P elements uniformly distributed throughout the triangular plate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3e-h, the Co, Fe, and P elements are uniformly distributed throughout the whole triangular plate.

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct hysteresis loop confirms mesoporous feature with Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 22.03 m² g⁻¹ and main pore size of 2.48 nm for Fe-CoP HTPAs; CoP TPAs show 17.62 m² g⁻¹ and 5.59 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated by the distinct hysteresis loop in the N₂ sorption adsorption-desorption isotherm (Figure S7a, Supporting Information), the Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit a mesoporous feature with a relatively high Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 22.03 m² g⁻¹ and the main pore size of 2.48 nm [38] while the BET surface area of the CoP TPAs is examined to be 17.62 m² g⁻¹ and the pore size is 5.59 nm (Figure S7b, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Co, Fe, P, C, O presence. High-resolution: Co 2p spin-orbit doublets at 778.6/793.6 eV (Co in FeCoP) and 781.5/797.5 eV (oxidized Co); Fe 2p at 707.2/720.4 eV (Fe in Fe-CoP), 712.9 eV (oxidized Fe); P 2p at 129.3, 130.1 eV (P in Fe-CoP), 133.7 eV (oxidized P).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a, the XPS spectrum of the as-prepared sample reveals the existence of Co, Fe, and P elements as well as C and O elements... The high-resolution XPS spectra of Co 2p (Figure 4b) exhibits two spin-obit doublets... at 778.6 and 793.6 eV can be indexed to the Co species in FeCoP. The other... at 781.5 and 797.5 eV corresponds to oxidized Co species... Fe 2p (Figure 4c) ... at 707.2 and 720.4 eV... P 2p core level spectrum (Figure 4d) reveals three main peaks at 129.3, 130.1, and 133.7 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 127.9 mF cm⁻², 2.9 times higher than CoP TPAs (43.7 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs exhibit a much higher Cdl of 127.9 mF cm⁻² , which is nearly 2.9 times that of CoP TPAs (43.7 mF cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: Smaller Rct and larger CPE-T compared to CoP TPAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As compared with CoP TPAs, a smaller Rct and larger CPE-T listed in Figure S10b in the Supporting Information can be observed with the mesoporous Fe-CoP HTPAs

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER: P element missing, Co 2p₃/₂ at 780.1 eV (Co in CoOOH), Fe 2p₃/₂ at 711.1 eV (Fe in FeOOH).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a red curve, the sample after OER test still exhibits Co, Fe elements, but the P element is missing... the Co 2p₃/₂ spectrum (Figure 4b, red curve) with a predominate peak located at 780.1 eV can be indexed to the Co species in CoOOH. The Fe 2p₃/₂ spectrum (Figure 4c, red curve) with a broad peak centered at about 711.1 eV can be assigned to Fe species in FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER: CoP peaks missing, new weak asymmetric peaks attributed to CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in XRD pattern (Figure S14, Supporting Information), the peaks of CoP are missing, while some new weak and asymmetric peaks attributed to the CoOOH appeared after the OER test

nodes.characterization_summary: After OER: lattice spacing d=0.25 nm corresponding to (100) plane of CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the HRTEM image in Figure S15 in the Supporting Information shows that some oxidation species are formed. The lattice spacing d of 0.25 nm can be determined to the (100) plane of CoOOH.
